Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

163 is not going to be easy! Sri Lanka have variety in their bowling and will back themselves to defend this. Oman will have to bat really well if they're to chase this down. Join us for the second essay in a bit.

The Oman bowlers did really well in the first 10 overs. Especially the likes of Kaleemullah and Fayyaz Ahmed. The bowlers to follow also did decently but it was the fielding that let them down. Had they taken their chances, maybe they would have kept Lanka below 140. Those chances cost a lot as their bowlers took a real pounding towards the end.

The start though was not that great for Lanka as they were 4 down for just the 51 and the run rate was also quite low. They found it quite difficult to get going on this wicket. Fernando though hung in there and once he got his eye in, he cashed in along with his skipper. Both added a 100-plus stand with both crossing the 50-run mark. Fernando was the mainstay and Shanaka provided the much-needed impetus his side needed.

42 runs from the last two overs have probably taken the game away from Oman! 160-plus on this wicket seems way too tough to chase down and Sri Lanka have their skipper and Fernando to thank because at one stage, it seemed like they would fall short of 130.

SRI LANKA (PLAYING XI) - Avishka Fernando, Bhanuka Rajapaksa, Dasun Shanaka (C), Chamika Karunaratne, Maheesh Theekshana, Dinesh Chandimal (WK), Kamindu Mendis, Nuwan Pradeep, Lahiru Kumara, Akila Dananjaya, Pathum Nissanka.
TOSS - Oman have won the toss and they have elected to bowl first.

The Indians have the Indian T20 League, Pakistan organized a domestic T20 tournament of their own after the New Zealand tour got cancelled. Everybody is preparing for the upcoming T20I WC and now the Lankans have arrived in the UAE to play a two-match T20I series. This is a good chance for them to get use to the conditions here and also get a fair idea of what their XI could be. They face Oman, who will also enjoy this experience. The Lankans are outright favorites and would love to win this 2-0 but even a solitary win for Oman could boost their confidence heading into the WC. Welcome to the coverage of the first T20I. Stay tuned for the toss in a bit.
